source_text: So when you say error is possibly caused by the fix itself, Or other things like regressions I feel as though these Codex agents are causing more harm than good in many cases, and they're consuming an awful lot of usage in the process so I'd like to have a scorecard or something where we keep track of these attempts in addition to the progress, we need to keep track of the failures because there have been an awful lot of them, it seems, and this whole thing has stayed flat the loss function has stayed flat since hours, when I thought we were going to have speed-ups so I want you to come up with some evidence that the approach we're using is actually working I think we've given every single possible clue about how the lean code works and yet these agents seem to me, unless I'm mistaken, to be grasping in the dark or am I mistaken because… Your reporting is giving me extremely mixed signals at one time, it seems like we're close at another time, it seems like the agents are making loads and loads of mistakes where are the mistakes coming from? Why are they even trying to ship? Code and test code when they're of such low confidence that it could actually work let me discuss that with you.

previous_reply_acts.text: (what happened) Each Codex agent hands its long run to a background job and ends its own turn. A watcher wakes me when the job exits, and I resume the agent. On every wake, my turn must end by restarting the watcher. On the A+B merge turn I did the merge and skipped that step. After that, every background job finished, but no wake came. The machine's load average has dropped to 5.7, which fits.

Voxterm should show them active again within a minute or two.
